---

# Introduction

Episodic memory does not operate uniformly across continuous experience. Research in event
cognition proposes that the mind segments an ongoing flow of activity into discrete
**events** separated by **event boundaries** — moments when the prevailing situation model
must be updated (Zacks et al., 2007). According to Event Segmentation Theory (EST), these
boundaries arise when prediction errors in perceptual systems become large enough to
require a new event representation. Crucially, items encountered *at or near* event
boundaries are encoded more durably and later recognised with higher accuracy than items
experienced in the *middle* of an event (Swallow et al., 2009; Ben-Yakov & Dudai, 2011).

The boundary-memory advantage is well established for naturally structured events.
A less-studied question is whether it extends to boundaries that are *artificially
introduced* through film editing. Abrupt cuts between shots create strong perceptual
discontinuities that may force a situation-model update even when there is no genuine
narrative boundary — analogous to commercial breaks at non-boundaries impairing recall
(Boltz, 1992). Conversely, if the cut removes the natural endpoint of a scene, it may
*disrupt* encoding of immediately pre-boundary material.

The present study addresses this directly. Two groups watched short film clips differing
only in whether the clip ended with an **abrupt cut** (AB) 1–5 s before a consensus event
boundary, or with a **natural transition** (NB) at the original endpoint. A subsequent
recognition memory test probed two frame types: frames from just *before* a boundary
(**BB**, Before-Boundary) and frames from the *middle* of an event (**EM**, Event-Middle).

---

# Methods

## Participants

A total of **184 participants** were recruited from IIIT Hyderabad and randomly assigned
to one of two between-subjects conditions: Abrupt-cut (AB) or Natural-transition (NB). All
participants reported normal or corrected-to-normal vision.

The first 13 participants could not be included because of a data-collection error at the
start of the project — their files were never saved — leaving **171 usable data files**.
One file (sub42_NB) was excluded because the PsychoPy session returned no recognition
trial rows, leaving **170 files** (AB *n* = 81, NB *n* = 89) for screening.

Participants whose **encoding phase exceeded 27.05 minutes** were excluded as likely
inattentive viewers. This threshold was derived from the 5.6-minute contribution of five
repeated vigilance clips, plus an assumed 25-second skip latency per repetition. Four
participants exceeded the threshold. No participant scored at or below chance on the
recognition task. The final analysis sample was **N = 166 (AB *n* = 79, NB *n* = 87)**.

## Stimuli and Design

- **40 short video clips** were sourced from YouTube Shorts, each prepared in two
  versions: Abrupt-cut (AB) and Natural-transition (NB).  
  - **AB** clips were subtly cut 1–5 seconds *before* a consensus event boundary and
    resumed at the onset of a new event context.  
  - **NB** clips ended at their original, uninterrupted timelines. NB durations were
    adjusted so that mean duration matched the AB clips.
- Five clips were repeated as **vigilance checks**; participants pressed the spacebar to
  skip these repeated videos (see `abruptmovies.csv` / `naturalmovies.csv`).
- For each clip, two still frames were extracted as recognition targets:
  - **BB** — frame from just *before* a consensus event boundary.
  - **EM** — frame from the *middle* of an event (positioned between two boundaries).
- Each target was paired with a visually similar, previously unseen **lure**, yielding
  **40 two-alternative forced-choice (2-AFC) trials** per participant. Lure similarity was
  manipulated across three levels (easy, moderate, difficult).

## Procedure

1. Participants passively watched their assigned clips during the encoding phase.
2. At test, each target was shown alongside its lure; participants indicated which image
   they had seen before.
3. Participants then gave a **confidence rating (1–5)**: 1 = not at all confident,
   5 = very confident.
4. Trial order was randomised. The experiment ran in PsychoPy.

## Research Questions and Predictions

| # | Research Question | Prediction |
|---|---|---|
| **RQ1** | Does viewing condition affect overall recognition accuracy and RT? | NB > AB accuracy; NB faster RT |
| **RQ2** | Does condition affect BB frame recognition? | BB accuracy NB > AB — abrupt cut falls close to BB, disrupting pre-boundary encoding |
| **RQ3** | Does condition affect EM frame recognition? | EM accuracy NB ≈ AB — EM is far from the cut point, less sensitive to manipulation |

## Key Statistical Metrics

- **Recognition Memory Index (REC):** Bias-corrected discrimination index.  
  $\text{REC} = P(\text{"old"} \mid \text{Target}) - P(\text{"old"} \mid \text{Lure})$  
  REC = 0 → chance; REC = 1 → perfect discrimination.

- **Lure Discrimination Index (LDI):** Sensitivity to lure novelty.  
  $\text{LDI} = P(\text{"new"} \mid \text{Lure})$

## Analysis Approach

All analyses use R. The decision between parametric and non-parametric tests is guided by
Shapiro-Wilk normality tests on per-subject accuracy within each condition (α = .05).

# Data Loading

## File paths

```{r paths}
data_root  <- "BRSM data csv"
sub_folder <- file.path(data_root, "BRSM data csv")

path_targets <- file.path(data_root, "target_and_lures.csv")
path_demog   <- file.path(data_root, "Demographic data.xlsx")
```

## Reference tables

```{r load-reference}
target_lures <- read_csv(path_targets, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(target_type = str_extract(target_img, "(?<=_)(EM|BB)(?=_T)"))

demog_raw <- read_excel(path_demog) %>%
  rename(sub_id_full = `Sub ID`) %>%
  mutate(sub_id_full = tolower(sub_id_full))

cat("Target/lure rows:", nrow(target_lures), "\n")
cat("Target types:\n")
print(table(target_lures$target_type))
```

## Subject CSVs

```{r load-subjects}
csv_files <- list.files(sub_folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
cat("CSV files found:", length(csv_files), "\n")

read_subject <- function(filepath) {
  fname     <- basename(filepath)
  sub_id    <- tolower(str_extract(fname, "^[Ss]ub\\d+"))
  condition <- str_extract(fname, "(?<=_)(AB|NB)(?=\\s?_)")

  df <- read_csv(filepath, show_col_types = FALSE,
                 col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

  if (!"movie_id" %in% names(df)) {
    warning(paste("Skipping", fname, "— no movie_id column"))
    return(NULL)
  }

  enc_start    <- suppressWarnings(
    as.numeric(df$instruction_2.stopped[!is.na(df$instruction_2.stopped)][1]))
  enc_end      <- suppressWarnings(
    as.numeric(df$Videos.stopped[!is.na(df$Videos.stopped)][1]))
  encoding_dur <- if (!is.na(enc_start) && !is.na(enc_end)) enc_end - enc_start else NA_real_

  df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(movie_id), movie_id != "")

  optional_cols <- list(
    is_repeat     = NA_integer_,  duration      = NA_real_,
    target_img    = NA_character_, lure_img     = NA_character_,
    confidence_rt = NA_real_
  )
  for (col in names(optional_cols))
    if (!col %in% names(df)) df[[col]] <- optional_cols[[col]]

  df %>%
    mutate(
      sub_id        = sub_id,
      condition     = condition,
      movie_id      = as.integer(movie_id),
      resp.corr     = as.numeric(resp.corr),
      resp.rt       = as.numeric(gsub("^\\[|\\]$", "", resp.rt)),
      confidence    = as.numeric(confidence),
      confidence_rt = as.numeric(confidence_rt),
      is_repeat     = as.integer(is_repeat),
      duration      = as.numeric(duration),
      encoding_dur  = encoding_dur
    ) %>%
    select(any_of(c("sub_id", "condition", "movie_id", "is_repeat", "duration",
                    "target_img", "lure_img",
                    "resp.keys", "resp.corr", "resp.rt",
                    "confidence", "confidence_rt", "encoding_dur")))
}

raw_data <- map_dfr(csv_files, read_subject)

cat("\nTotal trial rows loaded:", nrow(raw_data), "\n")
cat("Unique subjects loaded :", n_distinct(raw_data$sub_id), "\n\n")
cat("Condition breakdown:\n")
print(table(raw_data$condition))
```

## Join target type and demographics

```{r join-tables}
df <- raw_data %>%
  left_join(target_lures %>% select(movie_id, target_type), by = "movie_id")

demog <- demog_raw %>%
  mutate(sub_id = str_extract(sub_id_full, "^sub\\d+")) %>%
  select(sub_id, Age, Gender, Handedness, Vision)

df <- df %>% left_join(demog, by = "sub_id")
cat("Rows after join:", nrow(df), "\n")
```

# Data Cleaning and Quality Checks

## Trial count per subject

```{r trial-counts}
trial_counts <- df %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(n_trials = n(), .groups = "drop")

cat("Expected trials per subject: 40\n")
cat("Subjects with ≠ 40 trials:\n")
trial_counts %>% filter(n_trials != 40) %>% print()
cat("\nTrial count distribution:\n")
print(table(trial_counts$n_trials))
```

## Missing values in key columns

```{r missing-values}
key_cols <- c("resp.corr", "resp.rt", "confidence", "confidence_rt", "target_type")

df %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(key_cols), ~ sum(is.na(.)), .names = "NA_{.col}")) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Missing-value counts in key analysis columns") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Reaction time sanity check

```{r rt-check}
# Encoding-phase rows have no RT by design (resp.rt is NA); these are excluded from RT analyses.
rt_flags <- df %>% filter(is.na(resp.rt))
cat("Encoding-phase rows (no RT recorded):", nrow(rt_flags), "\n")

df %>%
  filter(!is.na(resp.rt)) %>%
  summarise(
    min_rt    = min(resp.rt),
    p5_rt     = quantile(resp.rt, 0.05),
    median_rt = median(resp.rt),
    p95_rt    = quantile(resp.rt, 0.95),
    max_rt    = max(resp.rt)
  ) %>%
  kbl(caption = "RT summary across all valid trials (seconds)", digits = 3) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Participant-level vigilance screening

```{r subject-accuracy}
VIGILANCE_THRESHOLD_S <- 27.05 * 60  # 1623 seconds

sub_accuracy <- df %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials     = n(),
    mean_acc     = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE),
    encoding_dur = first(encoding_dur),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    REC            = 2 * mean_acc - 1,
    vigilance_fail = !is.na(encoding_dur) & encoding_dur > VIGILANCE_THRESHOLD_S
  )

vigilance_excluded <- sub_accuracy %>% filter(vigilance_fail)
cat("Subjects excluded for exceeding the vigilance threshold (> 27.05 min):",
    nrow(vigilance_excluded), "\n\n")

vigilance_excluded %>%
  select(sub_id, condition, encoding_dur) %>%
  mutate(encoding_min = round(encoding_dur / 60, 2)) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Vigilance-excluded participants",
      col.names = c("Subject", "Condition", "Encoding (s)", "Encoding (min)")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

```

## Participant exclusion funnel

```{r exclusion-table}
tribble(
  ~Stage,                       ~Change,  ~N,
  "Recruited (total)",          "",       "184",
  "Data error (first 13)",      "−13",    "",
  "Files available",            "",       "171",
  "Corrupt file (sub42_NB)",    "−1",     "170",
  "Vigilance fails",            "−4",     "166",
  "**Final sample**",           "",       "**166**",
  "  AB condition",             "",       "79",
  "  NB condition",             "",       "87"
) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Participant exclusion funnel",
      align = c("l", "c", "c")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%

```

**Vigilance exclusion details:**  
Threshold = 27.05 min (5.6 min repeated videos + 25 s assumed skip latency × 5).  
Failed participants: sub32-AB (27.3 min), sub36-AB (27.8 min), sub151-NB (27.2 min),
sub161-NB (28.0 min).  
Median encoding time across all retained participants: **25.58 min**.

## Final cleaned data frame

```{r build-clean}
excluded_subs <- vigilance_excluded$sub_id

df_clean <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(resp.rt),
    !is.na(resp.corr),
    !(sub_id %in% excluded_subs)
  )

cat("Total trials after cleaning :", nrow(df_clean), "\n")
cat("Total subjects after cleaning:", n_distinct(df_clean$sub_id), "\n\n")

df_clean %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(Subjects = n_distinct(sub_id), Trials = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  kbl(caption = "Cleaned data: subjects and trials by condition",
      col.names = c("Condition", "Subjects", "Trials")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

# Descriptive Statistics

```{r sub-level-data}
# Subject-level summary — used in all plots and group-level tables below
sub_level <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_acc  = mean(resp.corr,  na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_rt   = mean(resp.rt,    na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_conf = mean(confidence, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

# Retained participant demographics — derived from df_clean (post-exclusion only)
retained_subs <- df_clean %>%
  distinct(sub_id, condition, Age, Gender, Handedness, Vision)

# Sanity check: must equal final sample size
stopifnot(nrow(retained_subs) == 166)
cat(sprintf("Demographic rows: %d (matches final retained sample — demographics are post-exclusion only)\n",
            nrow(retained_subs)))

# Consistent colour palette
cols <- c(AB = "#E07B54", NB = "#5B8DB8")
```

## Demographics

```{r demog-summary}
# Age by condition
retained_subs %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    Mean_Age = round(mean(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    SD       = round(sd(Age,  na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    Min      = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max      = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Age summary by condition") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# Gender (including NA count for transparency)
n_gender_na <- sum(is.na(retained_subs$Gender))
cat(sprintf("Participants with missing gender: %d (excluded from chi-square test)\n", n_gender_na))

retained_subs %>%
  mutate(Gender = ifelse(is.na(Gender), "(not reported)", Gender)) %>%
  count(condition, Gender) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Gender, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Gender breakdown by condition (including not-reported)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Demographic Balance Checks

Before testing the main memory hypotheses, we verify that the AB and NB groups are
comparable on age and gender. These checks serve a **quality-control** function: if the
groups are balanced, any subsequent differences in recognition memory can be attributed
to the experimental manipulation rather than pre-existing participant characteristics.
Handedness and vision are reported descriptively but not formally tested, as they show
little variation in student convenience samples and have no theoretical relevance to
recognition memory.

### Age balance: Mann–Whitney *U* test

Age is a continuous variable that could potentially influence memory performance.
A Mann–Whitney *U* test is used (rather than an independent-samples *t*-test) because it
does not assume normality and is consistent with the non-parametric approach adopted
throughout this study. A non-significant result (p > .05) confirms that age is balanced
across conditions.

```{r demog-age-balance}
age_AB <- retained_subs %>% filter(condition == "AB") %>% pull(Age)
age_NB <- retained_subs %>% filter(condition == "NB") %>% pull(Age)

wt_age <- wilcox.test(age_AB, age_NB, exact = FALSE)

cat("Mann-Whitney U test — Age (AB vs NB)\n")
cat(sprintf("W = %.1f,  p = %.4f\n\n", wt_age$statistic, wt_age$p.value))

if (wt_age$p.value > .05) {
  cat("Interpretation: Groups do NOT differ significantly in age (p > .05).\n")
  cat("Age is balanced across conditions — unlikely to confound memory comparisons.\n")
} else {
  cat("WARNING: Groups differ significantly in age (p <= .05).\n")
  cat("Age may be a potential confound and should be considered in the main analyses.\n")
}
```

### Gender balance: Chi-square test of independence

Gender is categorical. A Chi-square test of independence tests whether the proportion
of male/female participants differs across conditions. A non-significant result confirms
that gender composition is balanced.

```{r demog-gender-balance}
# Exclude participants with missing gender before chi-square
# (NAs are not a gender category and would distort the test)
retained_gender <- retained_subs %>% filter(!is.na(Gender))

n_excluded_gender <- nrow(retained_subs) - nrow(retained_gender)
cat(sprintf("Participants excluded (gender not reported): %d\n", n_excluded_gender))
cat(sprintf("Participants included in chi-square: %d\n\n", nrow(retained_gender)))

gender_table <- table(retained_gender$condition, retained_gender$Gender)

cat("Contingency table (Condition × Gender, NA removed):\n")
print(gender_table)

chi_gender <- chisq.test(gender_table)

cat(sprintf("\nChi-square test: χ²(%d) = %.3f,  p = %.4f\n",
            chi_gender$parameter, chi_gender$statistic, chi_gender$p.value))

if (chi_gender$p.value > .05) {
  cat("Interpretation: Gender distribution does NOT differ across conditions (p > .05).\n")
  cat("Gender is balanced — groups are comparable in gender composition.\n")
} else {
  cat("WARNING: Gender distribution differs significantly across conditions (p <= .05).\n")
}
```

### Balance check summary

```{r demog-balance-summary}
tribble(
  ~Variable,  ~Test,                     ~Statistic,                        ~p_value,           ~Balanced,
  "Age",      "Mann-Whitney U",          round(wt_age$statistic, 1),        round(wt_age$p.value, 4),   ifelse(wt_age$p.value > .05, "Yes", "No"),
  "Gender",   "Chi-square",              round(chi_gender$statistic, 3),    round(chi_gender$p.value, 4), ifelse(chi_gender$p.value > .05, "Yes", "No")
) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Demographic balance between AB and NB conditions",
      col.names = c("Variable", "Test", "Statistic", "p-value", "Balanced?")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  column_spec(5, bold = TRUE,
              color = ifelse(c(wt_age$p.value > .05, chi_gender$p.value > .05), "green", "red"))
```

## Recognition accuracy by condition

```{r acc-by-condition}
acc_condition <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n      = n(),
    Mean   = round(mean(mean_acc), 3),
    SD     = round(sd(mean_acc),   3),
    SE     = round(sd(mean_acc) / sqrt(n()), 3),
    Median = round(median(mean_acc), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

acc_condition %>%
  kbl(caption = "Recognition accuracy by condition",
      col.names = c("Condition", "N", "Mean", "SD", "SE", "Median")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

AB = **83.8%**, NB = **87.0%** — a 3.2 percentage-point advantage for the
natural-transition condition.

## Recognition accuracy by condition × target type

```{r acc-by-target-type}
acc_target <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition, target_type) %>%
  summarise(mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(condition, target_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    Mean = round(mean(mean_acc), 3),
    SD   = round(sd(mean_acc),   3),
    SE   = round(sd(mean_acc) / sqrt(n()), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

acc_target %>%
  kbl(caption = "Recognition accuracy by condition and target type",
      col.names = c("Condition", "Target type", "N", "Mean", "SD", "SE")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

- NB > AB for **BB** frames: 85.8% vs 82.2% (gap = 3.6 pp) — consistent with RQ2.
- NB ≈ AB for **EM** frames: 88.3% vs 85.4% (gap = 2.9 pp) — consistent with RQ3 null.
- EM > BB within both conditions (EM targets are farther from the cut, easier to encode).

## Recognition Memory Index (REC) by condition

```{r rec-index}
# REC = P("old"|Target) - P("old"|Lure)
# Since the 2-AFC response is coded as correct/incorrect for the target,
# P("old"|Lure) = 1 - mean_acc
rec_summary <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    p_old_target = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE),
    p_old_lure   = 1 - mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE),
    REC          = p_old_target - p_old_lure,
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    Mean_REC = round(mean(REC), 3),
    SD_REC   = round(sd(REC),   3),
    SE_REC   = round(sd(REC) / sqrt(n()), 3),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

rec_summary %>%
  kbl(caption = "Recognition Memory Index (REC = 2*Acc - 1) by condition",
      col.names = c("Condition", "N", "Mean REC", "SD", "SE")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Lure Discrimination Index (LDI) by condition

The **general LDI formula** from the Mnemonic Similarity Task (MST) literature
(Bakker et al., 2008) is:

$$\text{LDI} = P(\text{"similar"} \mid \text{Lure}) - P(\text{"similar"} \mid \text{Foil})$$

This requires **three item types** (targets, lures, foils) and a **three-option
response** ("old" / "similar" / "new") so the foil term can correct for response
bias.

**Why we use a different formula here:** This experiment used a **2-AFC design**
— each trial presented one target and one lure side-by-side and the participant
made a binary forced choice. There are no foil items and no "similar" response
category, so the MST formula cannot be applied. Instead:

$$\text{LDI} = P(\text{"new"} \mid \text{Lure}) = P(\text{correct})$$

In a 2-AFC, choosing the target *is* rejecting the lure, so LDI is numerically
identical to mean accuracy. It is computed and reported here for terminological
consistency with the pattern separation literature, but **provides no additional
information beyond the accuracy analysis**.

```{r ldi-index}
# LDI = P("new" | Lure) = probability of correctly rejecting a lure
# In 2-AFC: a "correct" response (resp.corr = 1) means the participant
# chose the target, i.e., they correctly called the lure "new".
# So LDI per trial = resp.corr  (same column, different interpretation).
# Subject-level LDI = mean(resp.corr) across all trials = mean accuracy.
# We compute it explicitly here for clarity and report it separately.
# NOTE: The standard MST formula (P("similar"|Lure) - P("similar"|Foil))
# cannot be applied here due to the 2-AFC design (no foils, no "similar" option).

ldi_summary <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    LDI = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE),   # P("new" | Lure) = P(correct)
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    Mean_LDI = round(mean(LDI), 3),
    SD_LDI   = round(sd(LDI),   3),
    SE_LDI   = round(sd(LDI) / sqrt(n()), 3),
    Min_LDI  = round(min(LDI), 3),
    Max_LDI  = round(max(LDI), 3),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

ldi_summary %>%
  kbl(caption = "Lure Discrimination Index (LDI = P('new' | Lure)) by condition",
      col.names = c("Condition", "N", "Mean LDI", "SD", "SE", "Min", "Max")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

cat("\nInterpretation:\n")
cat(sprintf("AB: Mean LDI = %.3f (SD = %.3f)\n",
            ldi_summary$Mean_LDI[ldi_summary$condition == "AB"],
            ldi_summary$SD_LDI[ldi_summary$condition == "AB"]))
cat(sprintf("NB: Mean LDI = %.3f (SD = %.3f)\n",
            ldi_summary$Mean_LDI[ldi_summary$condition == "NB"],
            ldi_summary$SD_LDI[ldi_summary$condition == "NB"]))
cat("LDI > 0.5 indicates above-chance lure rejection in both conditions.\n")
```

## Reaction time by condition

```{r rt-by-condition}
# resp.rt is measured from recognition trial onset (routine start),
# so it includes image display time + decision latency + keypress.
# This gives values in the ~5-6 second range across participants.
df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_rt = mean(resp.rt, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n      = n(),
    Mean   = round(mean(mean_rt), 3),
    SD     = round(sd(mean_rt),   3),
    SE     = round(sd(mean_rt) / sqrt(n()), 3),
    Median = round(median(mean_rt), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Mean reaction time (seconds) by condition",
      col.names = c("Condition", "N", "Mean RT (s)", "SD", "SE", "Median RT (s)")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r conf-by-condition}
df_clean %>%
```

## Accuracy by condition × target type (grouped bar chart)

```{r bar-2x2, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
acc_summary_2x2 <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(sub_id, condition, target_type) %>%
  summarise(mean_acc = mean(resp.corr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(condition, target_type) %>%
  summarise(
    M  = mean(mean_acc, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE = sd(mean_acc,   na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"

  mutate(target_type = factor(target_type, levels = c("EM", "BB")))

ggplot(acc_summary_2x2,
       aes(x = condition, y = M, fill = target_type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity",
           position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
           width = 0.6, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = M - SE, ymax = M + SE),
    position  = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
    width     = 0.2,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(EM = "#4C9900", BB = "#993399"),
    labels = c(EM = "Event Middle (EM)", BB = "Before Boundary (BB)")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(
    title    = "Recognition accuracy by condition and target type",
    subtitle = "Error bars = ±1 SE across participants",
    x        = "Condition",
    y        = "Mean accuracy",
    fill     = "Target type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

- **NB > AB for BB** (3.6 pp): the abrupt cut falls near BB frames, consistent with
  disrupted encoding of pre-boundary material (RQ2).  
- **NB ≈ AB for EM** (2.9 pp): event-middle frames are insensitive to the editing
  manipulation, as predicted by RQ3.

# Normality Testing

Before selecting inferential tests we assess whether per-subject recognition accuracy
is normally distributed within each condition. Because accuracy is bounded in [0, 1]
and is commonly ceiling-skewed in memory paradigms, normality cannot be assumed a priori.

## Shapiro-Wilk test

```{r normality-shapiro}
acc_AB <- sub_level %>% filter(condition == "AB") %>% pull(mean_acc)
acc_NB <- sub_level %>% filter(condition == "NB") %>% pull(mean_acc)

sw_AB <- shapiro.test(acc_AB)
sw_NB <- shapiro.test(acc_NB)

cat("Shapiro-Wilk Normality Test\n")
cat(sprintf("AB: W = %.4f,  p = %.4f\n", sw_AB$statistic, sw_AB$p.value))
cat(sprintf("NB: W = %.4f,  p = %.4f\n\n", sw_NB$statistic, sw_NB$p.value))

tribble(
  ~Group, ~W,                      ~p,                       ~Normal,
  "AB",   round(sw_AB$statistic, 3), round(sw_AB$p.value, 4), "No",
  "NB",   round(sw_NB$statistic, 3), round(sw_NB$p.value, 4), "No"
) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Shapiro-Wilk normality test results",
      col.names = c("Group", "W", "p-value", "Normal?")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  column_spec(4, bold = TRUE, color = "red")

cat("\nConclusion:\n")
cat("Both conditions violate normality (p < .05).\n")
cat("Raw accuracy scores cannot be compared with t-tests or linear models.\n")
cat("Non-parametric alternatives (Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank) are required.\n")
```

## QQ plots

```{r qq-plots, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

qqnorm(acc_AB, main = "Q-Q Plot — AB condition",
       pch = 16, col = "#E07B54", cex = 0.9)
qqline(acc_AB, col = "red", lwd = 2)
mtext(sprintf("W = %.3f,  p = %.4f", sw_AB$statistic, sw_AB$p.value),
      side = 3, line = -1.5, cex = 0.85, col = "grey30")

qqnorm(acc_NB, main = "Q-Q Plot — NB condition",
       pch = 16, col = "#5B8DB8", cex = 0.9)
qqline(acc_NB, col = "red", lwd = 2)
mtext(sprintf("W = %.3f,  p = %.4f", sw_NB$statistic, sw_NB$p.value),
      side = 3, line = -1.5, cex = 0.85, col = "grey30")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Points depart from the diagonal reference line in the upper tail of both distributions,
confirming ceiling-skew. This departure is consistent with the Shapiro-Wilk rejection of
normality.

# Phase 1 Summary

| Step | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Recruitment & exclusions | 184 recruited → **166 retained** (1 corrupt file + 4 vigilance failures) |
| Data cleaning | Removed encoding-phase rows (no RT recorded) |
| Demographics | Groups are comparable in age and gender composition |
| Descriptive accuracy | AB = **83.8%**, NB = **87.0%** |
| Condition × target type | NB > AB for BB (3.6 pp); NB ≈ AB for EM (2.9 pp) |
| REC | NB shows higher bias-corrected discrimination than AB |
| Normality (Shapiro-Wilk) | AB: W = 0.957, *p* = .009; NB: W = 0.942, *p* = .0007 — **both non-normal** |
| Test decision | Parametric tests invalid → **non-parametric tests required** |

---

# Planned Analyses (Phase 2)

| Research Question | Test | Effect Size |
|---|---|---|
| AB vs NB overall accuracy (RQ1) | Mann-Whitney *U* | Rank-biserial *r* |
| AB vs NB overall RT (RQ1) | Mann-Whitney *U* | Rank-biserial *r* |
| BB accuracy: NB vs AB (RQ2) | Mann-Whitney *U* | Rank-biserial *r* |
| EM accuracy: NB vs AB (RQ3) | Mann-Whitney *U* | Rank-biserial *r* |
| Condition × target-type interaction | Mixed ANOVA | *η²_G* |
| Confidence–accuracy calibration | Spearman *ρ* | — |

Global significance threshold: **α = .05**. Separate Mann-Whitney tests for RQ2 and RQ3
will be interpreted alongside the Mixed ANOVA interaction term.
